items.title: Three arrested at anti-austerity student protest
items.author: Léo Vallet David
items.excerpt: Thousands of students protested on Friday over their discontent with austerity measures, eventually leading to three arrests and clashes with the police.
items.leadExcerpt: On Friday, Nov. 13, thousands of students rallied at Square-Victoria around 2 p.m. to protest austerity measures imposed on the province’s CEGEPs and universities. The crowd was estimated at between 75,000 and 100,000 people, according to reports from both La Presse and Radio-Canada. The SPVM did not calculate the exact number of protesters. The protest ended at around 5 p.m. with three arrests and eight mischiefs — a legal term describing property damage or destruction, property rendered dangerous, useless, inoperative or ineffective, obstructed, or interrupting or interfering with its lawful use — confirmed by the Montreal police (SPVM).

items.title: More than half of Quebecers are unsatisfied with Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, according to recent poll
items.author: Léo Vallet David
items.excerpt: A recent Pallas Data poll puts St-Pierre Plamondon’s approval rating at 23 per cent, an unwelcome sign for a newly elected minority government
items.leadExcerpt: The results are even worse on the Island of Montreal, where the Parti Québécois (PQ) won two seats — including St-Pierre Plamondon’s. Only 14 per cent of of respondents were satisfied with his government, compared to 62 per cent who were not. In the greater Montreal area — which encompasses Laval, the north and south shores — that number goes down to 50 per cent saying they’re unsatisfied with the performance so far and 26 per cent said they’re satisfied. On Oct. 5, the PQ carried 26 ridings in both the north and south shores.

items.title: Abolir ou réformer Santé Québec ?
items.author: Médéric Dens
items.excerpt: Deux ans après la création de Santé Québec, quoi garder et quoi réformer ? Ce qui s’annonçait comme un projet mettant à l’avant-plan l’efficience, semble pourtant ajouter un poids sur la bureaucratie dans un ministère déjà alourdi.
items.leadExcerpt: Deux ans après la création de Santé Québec, quoi garder et quoi réformer ? Ce qui s’annonçait comme un projet mettant à l’avant-plan l’efficience, semble pourtant ajouter un poids sur la bureaucratie dans un ministère déjà alourdi. Le premier ministre du Québec, Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, avait promis d’abolir Santé Québec lors de la plus récente campagne. Ce dernier semble pourtant se rétracter et parle désormais d’une « réforme », en ne conservant que les éléments fonctionnels.

items.leadExcerpt: As we enter November, I am confident that many McGillians share the dread I feel, knowing that the days of sitting on Lower Field with only a light sweater are behind us. As a Canadian, I don’t believe I will ever fully acclimatise to this weather, even two decades in. Facing this impending drop in temperature and the relegation of warm weather to the realm of the fever dream, I decided a rewatch of Sterling Point (2026) was in order. How better to hold onto Canada’s summers than by climbing right back into that environment, letting this well-made, sunny, coming-of-age show take over my screen once again?

items.title: How a student-led movement prevailed in Serbia’s election
items.author: Léo Vallet David
items.excerpt: After months of protests and years of frustration, Serbian students have prevailed, electing 140 pro-student candidates to the National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia on Oct. 25.
items.leadExcerpt: The newly created Student List (SL) party won 140 seats, while President Aleksandar Vučić’s United Serbia party won 103, giving the SL a majority of 30 seats in Serbia’s parliament. This shift in Serbian politics marks a new era, with young protesters having led the charge to remove Aleksandar Vučić from power. Vučić, who was Serbia’s prime minister from 2014 to 2017, was first elected president in 2017 with 56 per cent of the votes. He won the presidential election again in 2022, though his party narrowly lost its majority in parliament, which it won back in 2023.

items.title: Why young people should watch more films like Persepolis
items.author: Chloé Etienne
items.excerpt: As a Concordia student minoring in film studies, I am fortunate to have access to a wide range of films that enrich and educate me on a daily basis. During my film history class this week, I had the chance to watch Persepolis, a French animated film adapted from the
items.leadExcerpt: As a Concordia student minoring in film studies, I am fortunate to have access to a wide range of films that enrich and educate me on a daily basis. During my film history class this week, I had the chance to watch Persepolis, a French animated film adapted from the autobiographical graphic novel by Marjane Satrapi, a Franco-Iranian artist. Directed by Satrapi herself and Vincent Paronnaud, Persepolis explores Marjane’s childhood in Tehran, which is marked by the 1979 Islamic Revolution, the mullahs’ regime, the oppression suffered by women and the Iran-Iraq War. But beyond political and social issues, the film portrays resilience and the determination to push through and fight for one’s rights.

items.title: Peut-on encore posséder de la culture ?
items.author: Maxence Gibault-Renault
items.excerpt: GTA VI sera bien vendu en version physique, mais sans disque, avec simplement un code de téléchargement dans la jaquette. (Photo : Maxence Gibault-Renault) Tous les pans de l’industrie culturelle sont concernés. La digitalisation conduit les éditeurs à se passer des supports
items.leadExcerpt: Tous les pans de l’industrie culturelle sont concernés. La digitalisation conduit les éditeurs à se passer des supports physiques, parfois au détriment de l’utilisateur, contraint de ne plus posséder. « On a commencé à observer cela au début des années 2000 avec la création d’iTunes par Apple. Avant même les plateformes de visionnement en ligne, on vendait des chansons, mais les conditions d’utilisation précisaient déjà qu’il s’agissait d’une permission d’utilisation, et non d’une vente équivalente à celle d’un produit physique », explique Guy-Philippe Wells, chercheur au Laboratoire de recherche sur la découvrabilité et les transformations des industries culturelles à l’ère du commerce électronique de l’UQAM.

items.title: The kids are not alright: the youth unemployment problem in Canada
items.author: Kasi Peri
items.excerpt: According to the 2026 federal budget, Canada’s youth unemployment rate has hit 13.7 per cent this year. As unemployment numbers continue to increase for this age group, university and government programs have stepped in to try and address the problem.
items.leadExcerpt: According to the 2026 federal budget, Canada’s youth unemployment rate has hit 13.7 per cent this year. As unemployment numbers continue to increase for this age group, university and government programs have stepped in to try and address the problem. Statistics Canada’s Daily Labour Survey found that youth unemployment, which measures people aged 15–29, “rose 0.7 percentage points to 13.7% in October.” A TD Economics study also noted that unemployment for teenagers had increased. Unemployment rates for this particular age group are affected by limited job availability, especially in service industries, and the pandemic, according to data collected.

items.title: QUICKSPIN: Lil Baby — FRESH
items.author: Aidan Flanagan
items.excerpt: Lil Baby has been a household name in the hip-hop genre since 2018, largely thanks to his breakout hit “Yes Indeed.” Gone, however, are the days when a Lil Baby verse was a coveted commodity.
items.leadExcerpt: Lil Baby’s studio albums have failed to garner much attention, and it has never been clearer than on his latest record. FRESH is far from an apt title, as not a single track on this record feels fresh by any means. The intro track, “Top Uh It,” begins so abruptly that it feels as though the album began right in the middle of its own runtime, with the rapper seeming almost unable to keep up with the instrumental. The lyrics are about exactly what every other Lil Baby song has ever been about: money, cars and clothes.

items.leadExcerpt: Dove Cameron’s second studio album, FINAL GIRL, is her most confessional record yet. Vulnerability takes the stage in multiple forms as she explores the different makeups of the cinematic final girl — the one who conquers despite the mess. Cameron opens with “silver screen baby,” a soft ballad exposing a desperation to leave the Hollywood spotlight behind. The piano and strings create an atmosphere that drags listeners into the same emotionality whirling in her heart.

items.leadExcerpt: Good news for Bishop’s they now have three new master’s programs to consider. Bishop’s University has partnered with the Smith School of Business at Queen’s University to provide eligible Williams School of Business students with a faster pathway into post-grad study. This provides students with three different pathways into the International Business (Kingston), Management Analytics (Toronto), and Finance (Beijing) programs. Applicants can be nominated by Bishop’s in their final year of study. A nomination ensures that applicants won’t have to pay any fees and will be guaranteed an interview regarding the program and their future goals with a member of the Smith program team. You must still meet the requirements for your chosen degree, but you’ll receive $5,000 off your tuition.

items.leadExcerpt: As we approach the middle of the semester, students are feeling the pressure of exams, papers, readings, assignments and so much more. You likely find yourself trapped in the library for hours on end, staring at screens and attempting to dwindle down the long lists of mid-semester tasks. As important as it is to apply yourself, expand your mind and focus on studies, it is necessary to find a healthy balance. But how do you find balance when all you can focus on is the laundry list of tasks to complete? The answer is simpler than we make it out to be. Give some time back to yourself and take a break.

items.leadExcerpt: With the temperatures nearing 20°C in Sherbrooke in November, it’s the kind of weather that makes you check the date. So, with the rising winter temperatures, it feels fitting that Bishop’s offered a screening of YUMI – The Whole World, which highlights the devastating effects climate change has on the world, especially in the Pacific. YUMI shows that the signs of a changing climate are harder to take in stride. In Vanuatu, heavy rain can topple papaya trees and damage the food families grow. Along Fiji’s coast, rising seas and erosion are washing away some communities, and forcing others to move inland.

items.title: Bring Back The Gait
items.author: Arianna Koutrias
items.excerpt: When I started at Bishop’s, there was only one weekly occurrence that never changed: spending our night at The Gait. I’m not sure how this routine became so embedded in our Bishop’s culture, but it’s something unique and special to the school we call home for a few years. From
items.imageCredit: Photo : Mario Hains / CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
items.leadExcerpt: When I started at Bishop’s, there was only one weekly occurrence that never changed: spending our night at The Gait. I’m not sure how this routine became so embedded in our Bishop’s culture, but it’s something unique and special to the school we call home for a few years. From theme nights to specialty drinks, The Gait has become a place to look forward to on a Thursday night after a gruelling week of classes and studying. This year, there is an undeniable shift in The Gait’s popularity, as many students are no longer “gait-bound” on their nights out, specifically first-year students. I am unsure how this decline occurred; are first-year students just not going out anymore? While party life has been severely diminished at Bishop’s, the weekly Gait nights are something we never thought would change. It was, and always has been, a place that unites our student community. It also raises questions about the memories the next generation of Bishop’s students is missing out on.

items.title: La génération Z et le retour des médias physiques
items.author: Simone Gingras
items.excerpt: La génération Z semble s’intéresser de plus en plus aux technologies des dernières décennies. Les photos prises sur pellicule, les caméras numériques et les iPod sont de plus en plus présents sur les fils d’actualité. Pourquoi cet intérêt pour les médias rétro ?
items.sourceImageCredit: Photo : Alex Salcedo et Linus Bossardt
items.leadExcerpt: La génération Z semble s’intéresser de plus en plus aux technologies des dernières décennies. Les photos prises sur pellicule, les caméras numériques et les iPod sont de plus en plus présents sur les fils d’actualité. Pourquoi cet intérêt pour les médias rétro ? « Avec l’avancée rapide des technologies, il est normal que l’humain ait une résistance au changement », explique la doctorante en communication à l’Université du Québec à Montréal (UQAM) Simone Courville, qui se spécialise dans la nostalgie et les médias sociaux. Elle remarque que le numérique est aujourd’hui conçu pour l’instantanéité et donne l’exemple des médias sociaux, de l’écoute en continu ou des plateformes d’écoute de musique, qui sont accessibles partout et rapidement.

items.leadExcerpt: Marie-Eve Poitras, infirmière, professeure agrégée à l’Université de Sherbrooke et chercheuse au Centre de recherche et d’innovation du Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean, reçoit le Prix de chercheur de l’année en médecine de famille 2026. Une belle reconnaissance pour la recherche régionale. Les travaux de Marie-Eve Poitras ont été récompensé ce 12 novembre à Toronto, dans le cadre du Forum en médecine familiale du Collège des médecins de famille du Canada. Ils se démarquent notamment par sa volonté de placer les patientes et les patients au cœur des soins de première ligne. « Je crois que c’est la façon dont je travaille en équipe, mais également la façon dont j’intègre la perspective des patients dans les projets qu’on fait », explique la principale concernée. La chercheuse souhaite ainsi contribuer à améliorer les pratiques et à mieux répondre aux besoins de la population.

items.leadExcerpt: Dans plusieurs municipalités du Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean, plus de la moitié des personnes seules n’atteignent pas le revenu nécessaire pour sortir de la pauvreté. C’est ce que révèle une étude de l’Institut de recherche et d’informations socioéconomiques (IRIS), publiée le 27 octobre. Parmi les 15 municipalités étudiées, neuf comptent plus de la moitié de leurs personnes seules sous le seuil du revenu viable. Le revenu viable couvre les besoins essentiels et prévoit une marge de manœuvre pour faire face aux imprévus. Il va ainsi au-delà du seuil de pauvreté traditionnel. Pour une personne seule, le revenu viable annuel varie de 39 289 $ à Roberval à 44 048 $ à Saint-Fulgence.

items.title: Quand l’intelligence artificielle fait une erreur, qui est responsable?
items.author: Ève Thibodeau
items.excerpt: Que ce soit en retravaillant vos travaux scolaires, en corrigeant vos courriels ou, encore, en vous assistant à titre d’agent conversationnel pour une entreprise, l’intelligence artificielle (IA) est susceptible de commettre des erreurs.
items.leadExcerpt: Dans l’affaire Moffatt c. Air Canada, l’agent conversationnel d’Air Canada a offert une réduction post-achat à M. Moffatt en raison d’une urgence familiale, contrairement aux politiques de l’entreprise. Dans son jugement, le tribunal lui donne gain de cause et tient Air Canada responsable en établissant que le service à la clientèle automatisé ne dispense pas une société de ses obligations. Le tribunal a conclu qu’Air Canada avait engagé sa responsabilité en ne prenant pas les mesures raisonnables afin d’assurer l’exactitude des renseignements fournis par son agent conversationnel.

items.leadExcerpt: Ce fut une longue campagne électorale de 39 jours au Québec cet automne. Avec cinq partis en lice, les électeurs ont dû composer avec cinq plateformes politiques, des promesses quotidiennes et une couverture médiatique soutenue pendant toute la durée de la campagne. Le 5 octobre dernier, les personnes québécoises ont élu un gouvernement minoritaire du Parti québécois (PQ) dirigé par Paul St-Pierre Plamondon. Avec 28 % des suffrages exprimés, mais près de 47 % des sièges à l’Assemblée nationale, le PQ forme un gouvernement, malgré le plus faible pourcentage de votes obtenu par un parti gagnant dans l’histoire du Québec. En seulement quatre ans, le parti est passé de 3 à 60 députés, mettant fin aux huit années au pouvoir de la Coalition Avenir Québec (CAQ). Pour la CAQ, il s’agit d’une défaite historique. Bien que le parti ait obtenu 13 % des voix, il n’a fait élire aucun député à l’Assemblée nationale.

items.leadExcerpt: L’intelligence artificielle (IA) s’impose dans de nombreux domaines, qu’ils soient universitaires, culturels ou politiques. À quel moment doit-on l’utiliser? Remplacera-t-elle certains emplois? Représente-t-elle un risque pour la cybersécurité? Ces questions sont légitimes et le milieu de la culture et des arts est particulièrement touché par ces enjeux. Tout d’abord, distinguons un locateur d’un locataire. Selon le Code civil du Québec (C.c.Q.), le locateur est la personne qui fournit l’appartement. En d’autres mots, c’est le propriétaire. Le locataire est la personne qui habite dans l’appartement en fournissant un paiement mensuel au propriétaire. Il est possible d’avoir plusieurs locataires ou personnes habitant au sein d’un même appartement.

items.leadExcerpt: Take a second to listen to your surroundings. What can you hear? Perhaps it is the loud hum of the metro as you take the green line to school. Or maybe you’re reading this edition of The Plant in a busy cafe, the familiar hiss of coffee machines tickling your eardrums. Wherever we go, we are bound to be enveloped in an array of sounds — the scratching of pen against paper, the strident screech of your alarm clock, leaves crunching underfoot, planes roaring overhead.

items.title: Math, now, … Prof. Taimiņa’s Crochet Lesson
items.author: Charlie Reuter
items.excerpt: Do you remember your high school teacher telling you that the angles in a triangle always sum to 180°? (When I asked this at the Plant office, almost all hands went up.) Well, your teacher didn’t tell the truth. Those angles can sum up to pretty much anything you like. To see
items.leadExcerpt: Do you remember your high school teacher telling you that the angles in a triangle always sum to 180°? (When I asked this at the Plant office, almost all hands went up.) Well, your teacher didn’t tell the truth. Those angles can sum up to pretty much anything you like. To see why, grab some yarn and a slightly surprising but revolutionary mathematical tool: the crochet hook. This story begins in Ancient Greece, with a textbook: Euclid’s Elements. Spanning 13 volumes, it’s an impressive attempt to rigorously prove the field of mathematics as it was known at the time, with only the ruler and the compass for tools. In order to prove mathematical theorems, Euclid had to start somewhere. He settled on five obviously true statements, or “axioms,” from which he was able to derive all other theorems. One axiom, for example, is “all right angles are equal.” An immense success, the Elements remained the leading mathematical textbook up until the early 19th century.

items.leadExcerpt: When people talk about football, the NFL is often the first league that comes to mind. From the Super Bowl to some of the biggest names in sports, American football gets plenty of attention. But just north of the border, there is another league that deserves a spot in the conversation: the Canadian Football League. The CFL might not have the same international profile as the NFL, but that does not mean it has nothing to offer. For fans who have never watched a Canadian football game, or who only tune in for the Grey Cup, there are plenty of reasons to give the league a chance.

items.leadExcerpt: Depuis le 18 septembre 2026, un sujet d’actualité prime sur nos médias et nos réseaux sociaux. Le mouvement lycéen de 2026 en France soulève plusieurs débats dans les sphères politiques. Que se soit des vidéos de citoyens déguisés en Captain America ou des extraits d’un orchestre qui rythme la marche des manifestants, il met surtout en lumière des dénonciations universelles et la violence choquante à l’encontre de jeunes étudiants du corps policier. Les étudiants marchent contre les conditions d’enseignements et de scolarité: pas assez de profs, des horaires scolaires insoutenables et des salles de classes en ruine. Ils militent également pour la suppression de l’application d’admission aux études supérieures Parcoursup, une plateforme longuement critiquée pour son manque de transparence au niveau des critères d’admissibilité et sa restriction de places disponibles. En 2025, près de 39 000 candidats n’avaient reçu aucune proposition d’universités à la fin de la procédure, soit 6,5% des demandeurs selon les calculs du Monde.

items.title: Vacancy and the Rooftop Farming Culture of Montreal

items.excerpt: In my sculpture class, I recently built an interactive sculpture or what is essentially just a suggestion box, that asked a simple question I myself could not answer: “Quel type d’aménagement devrait-on faire ici?”. The idea was for visitors to slip a note with their request
items.leadExcerpt: The machine asks about aménagement but it answers with phrases that are about développement. Aménagement comes from ménager, to manage a household in French. How can we picture vacancy differently, not by aluminum gates and a lack of development or as places to be urbexed but as homes that haven’t been cared for enough? The rooftop-farming movement in Montreal differs from conventional development, because it is more of an aménagement: re-using and re-arranging the overlooked spaces into places full of life.

items.title: Who Has Health? Reading Vita: Life in a Zone of Social Abandonment
items.author: Martin Kaloshi
items.excerpt: “The kids are all sick; rain passes through the plastic. Who has health? Health nobody has. Every day we are ill, all kinds of illnesses, it is never good. There is no medical aid. Only if one has money for the bus and gets in line early in the morning and waits till late at
items.leadExcerpt: These words are José Duarte’s, taken from anthropologist João Biehl’s Vita: Life in a Zone of Social Abandonment. To make space for a new tourist centre, the government kicked José, his wife, and their four children out of the city’s historic district. They live on the outskirts of Salvador, Brazil, in a hut made of plastic bags. While they are covered by Brazil’s universal healthcare system on paper, José explains that at the medical office, he is only made to sign forms that never get back to him. He and his neighbours are stressed sick by the lack of housing and jobs, safety concerns, and growing police violence in their area. They feel the government has failed them, and that they’ve failed their children.

items.title: “You do not have to be Good”: On the Nature of Being
items.author: The editorial team
items.excerpt: Mauersegler By Léo-Paul Samuel Robert Chloe Bercovitz Co-Editor in Chief Among the bleaker moments, in which I feel less than myself, I cannot help but resort to nature. Because, to me, to be outside is to be free. I am unconfined. I feel small — as big, beautiful things nestle
items.leadExcerpt: “You do not have to be good. You do not have to walk on your knees for a hundred miles through the desert, repenting. You only have to let the soft animal of your body love what it loves.” This mantra of mine is echoed from her 1986 poem Wild Geese. It becomes easier to accept oneself, only upon stepping outside of the world we have created for ourselves. Our very best tool for perspective is natural: it is nature. And what a comfort it is to know that time and time again, the human race will forever have the same refuge!

items.leadExcerpt: Girlies, what jackets are we wearing this winter? Those shoes are so last season! This is the skirt of the summer! Red is in right now When will it stop? Fashion is, has been, and will forever be a never ending cycle of trends, shortening by the decade, and with social media turning all fashion fast, even quality and style become momentary fads. It is not new for fashion to resemble a social uniform–think of big frilly Victorian dresses, or Y2K layers. Merriam-Webster defines the term fashion as “the prevailing style during a particular time” and “the business of creating and selling clothes in new styles.” Magazines, such as Vogue, ELLE and Marie Claire, have been reporting on said fashion tendencies for well over a century, feeding into our homogenous ways.

items.title: At the Altar of AO3
items.author: The editorial team
items.excerpt: Once a week, I sit on a wooden bench to feel a little less lonely. No matter if the sun is setting or if the world is getting colder, it will always be there for me, just waiting for me to sit back down. When I eventually do, as I always will, the beats of a wellworn story
items.leadExcerpt: Once a week, I sit on a wooden bench to feel a little less lonely. No matter if the sun is setting or if the world is getting colder, it will always be there for me, just waiting for me to sit back down. When I eventually do, as I always will, the beats of a wellworn story envelop me. However, my pews are not placed within the confines of an institution; rather, they exist in spaces carved out by fellow fans on the internet— my fandom. Religion, like all socially constructed concepts, has a purpose for its existence; it speaks to human beings’ various needs. Religion serves to instill a sense of meaning to life, a place to feel close to our community, to gather and to learn from others. More importantly, especially for the comparison I am preparing to draw, it also serves as a common ground for people to understand each other, a springboard for other conversations to be had. All of which has become rarer and rarer as religion becomes further and further removed from most of our lives and loses its place as a cultural touchstone.

items.title: The Stories That Grow With Us
items.author: Sibora Dibra
items.excerpt: via HS Insider Sibora Dibra Arts and Culture Editor “All grown-ups were once children but only few of them remember it.” – Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, The Little Prince Once upon a time, a child drew a boa constrictor swallowing an elephant whole. A grown-up, peering over their
items.leadExcerpt: Once upon a time, a child drew a boa constrictor swallowing an elephant whole. A grown-up, peering over their shoulder to look at the very same drawing, saw a hat. Somewhere along the way, we trade imagination for the ordinary, the fantastical for the sensible. Our juvenile hunger for the surreal dissipates as time inevitably unfolds, leaving behind the elusive ghost of a childhood we’ve outgrown. When I first read Antoine de Saint-Exupéry’s The Little Prince, I was quickly captivated by the prince’s travels, particularly by his encounter with the Fox, who taught six-year-old me that the essential is invisible to the eye. Upon revisiting the novel as an emerging adult, however, I found myself paying less attention to the prince and more to each newly discovered planet’s residents: the king, the vain, the drunk, the businessman, the lamplighter and the geographer. Each represents, respectively, ego, vanity, alienation, greed, responsibility, and knowledge.

items.leadExcerpt: Après douze ans de carrière et trois participations aux Jeux olympiques, la judokate québécoise Catherine Beauchemin-Pinard a annoncé sa retraite sportive le 5 novembre dernier. Son parcours illustre les défis de la transition vers une vie sans sport de haut niveau. À 32 ans, Catherine Beauchemin-Pinard a déjà derrière elle une carrière remarquable : une médaille de bronze aux Jeux olympiques de Tokyo en 2021, deux médailles d’argent aux Championnats du monde seniors et trois participations olympiques. Le 7 octobre dernier, à Bakou, elle a disputé sa dernière compétition internationale. « Je voulais faire une dernière compétition, vivre un peu tout une dernière fois », précise-t-elle.

items.title: Albertans may have voted to stay in Canada, but they still have grievances
items.author: Matthew Johnson
items.excerpt: Alberta voted resoundingly in favour of remaining in Canada, so much so that the results are now one of the clearest majorities ever found in a secession referendum globally, with nearly 75 per cent supporting the remain side.
items.leadExcerpt: But whether to remain part of Canada was only one of 10 questions asked of Albertans on Oct. 19. It was also added later to the already planned referendum after Alberta Premier Daniel Smith lowered the barrier to entry to get the question on the ballot. The other nine questions focused on expanding Alberta’s immigration powers and broader constitutional issues like Senate reform and judicial appointments. While the sovereignty question was resoundingly clear, the other nine show Albertans are still not satisfied with their place in the Confederation — though not as much as Smith would like them to be.

items.leadExcerpt: Face à la crise climatique, au coût de la vie et à l’accès difficile à la propriété, certain·e·s jeunes cyniques ont le sentiment que leur avenir sera moins enviable que le présent. Si certain·e·s doutent des possibilités qui s’offrent à eux et à elles, d’autres croient encore pouvoir changer les choses. Comment cette peur nourrit-elle le défaitisme et le « à quoi bon ? » Inversement, comment permet-elle de faire renaître une nouvelle sorte d’espoir des centres ? Les statistiques s’accumulent : un 4 ½ à plus de 2 000 dollars par mois à Montréal, un 3 ½ à 1 500 dollars par mois à Gaspé La crise du logement continue de sévir à Montréal, mais aussi partout au Québec et dans d’autres pays dans le monde. En raison des canicules, des feux de forêt et des désastres naturels à répétition, sans parler des requins au rocher Percé, l’environnement est une source d’anxiété pour plusieurs jeunes. Malgré ce contexte difficile, est-il juste d’affirmer que ces dernier·ère·s sont devenus cyniques ?

Si l’accord est conclu, les détails juridiques restent toutefois à définir. Sur le Web québécois, ce flou diplomatique a néanmoins immédiatement cédé la place à une vague d’enthousiasme humoristique. De nombreuses plateformes ont alors recensé les réactions de Canadiens faisant des plaisanteries sur les voyages, la culture et le mode de vie européen sur les réseaux sociaux, parmi lesquels Instagram, TikTok ou encore X.

items.leadExcerpt: Souffler sur un feu peut l’éteindre comme l’attiser. On peut aussi refuser d’y toucher et le priver d’air, au risque de le laisser couver sous la cendre. Face à la théorie du « grand remplacement », selon laquelle une élite organiserait le remplacement de la population française blanche et chrétienne par une population venant des pays du sud, noire, maghrébine et musulmane. La classe politique française hésite entre ces deux gestes. Popularisée par l’essayiste Renaud Camus, cette idée de « grand remplacement » est « sans aucune ambiguïté xénophobe et complotiste », selon l’historienne Valérie Igounet, et sa composante raciale est « au cœur » de la théorie, pour l’historien Nicolas Bancel.

items.leadExcerpt: Un jeudi soir, il y a deux semaines, alors que je m’apprêtais à me coucher, un déferlement de messages de la part de quelques amis inonde mon téléphone. Mes yeux luttant encore contre le sommeil, je lis la publication qu’ils m’ont envoyée : « AO3 n’est pas disponible à cause d’une période d’entretien. » Jusque-là, je ne m’inquiète pas – ça arrive de temps à autre. Puis, quelques lignes plus bas, je vois le véritable coupable de cet affolement général. Au lieu des deux à douze heures habituelles d’interruption de service, le site prévoit un mois d’arrêt complet.

Cependant, lorsque des professeur·e·s de McGill nous déclarent ouvertement avoir utilisé l’IA pour agrémenter leurs diapositives, ou bien pour générer leurs exemples pédagogiques, la question persiste : quelle devrait être la place de l’IA au sein de l’Université McGill ?

items.leadExcerpt: Depuis que l’équipe éditoriale a choisi la résistance comme thème de cette édition, mon cerveau vit dans la plus grande agonie. Matin, midi et soir, sous la douche, à la vaisselle, du premier café à la dernière tisane, ma bouche ne peut s’empêcher de chantonner (et de hurler parfois) les mots de France Gall : « Résiste ! » Ce ne sont ni la Seconde Guerre mondiale ni aucun autre célèbre conte de résistance qui me sont venus à l’esprit. Ni l’Ukraine, la Palestine, le Soudan, le Congo, les manifestations contre la vie chère, la déforestation, le braconnage, les Rohingyas, l’Iran, la banalisation de l’extrême droite, le recul des droits à l’avortement et de la justice reproductive, les femmes en Afghanistan, la corporatisation de notre société, l’IA Non. C’est France Gall.

items.title: Êtes-vous Queer ?
items.author: Sixtine Nicolaÿ
items.excerpt: Un mot pour résister à la binarité.
items.leadExcerpt: L’utilité de ce mot réside dans sa capacité à être assez vague et ouvert à différentes interprétations. Les personnes qui se disent queer n’ont pas forcément les mêmes explications sur la raison qui les pousse à utiliser ce terme. Il est même à l’origine de divisions au sein de la communauté. Il est donc compliqué de le définir de manière arrêtée, mais il est tout de même possible d’en comprendre les différents usages. Pour comprendre le sens actuel du terme, il faut revenir à son utilisation initiale. « Queer » est un terme anglais qui signifie « étrange ». Aux 19e et 20e siècle, il était utilisé comme une injure afin de qualifier les hommes homosexuels, ceux-ci étant donc considérés comme bizarres – « queer ». Ainsi, il s’agit bien à la base d’une insulte homophobe très péjorative, en tout cas dans la bouche de personnes qui n’étaient pas homosexuelles.

items.title: Et si on parlait de la mort ?
items.author: Laurence Drouin
items.excerpt: OISEAU : une pièce qui dit les vérités qu’on préfère taire.
items.leadExcerpt: On porte des chandails à l’effigie de chanteurs décédés, on continue d’enseigner les théories de grands penseurs anciens, mais pourquoi est-il si difficile de parler de la mort de nos proches ? La mort semble occuper une place importante dans notre culture et notre histoire, mais elle demeure un sujet délicat quand elle touche notre entourage. Cet étrange paradoxe est soulevé par les personnages de la pièce de théâtre OISEAU d’Anna Nozière. Ce spectacle a ouvert la deuxième édition du festival international La mèche courte, qui se déroule du 4 au 8 novembre à Montréal et qui a pour but d’initier les jeunes au théâtre. OISEAU a été présentée en France en 2023 devant plus de 25 000 enfants, comme l’explique la coprésidente du festival, Mélanie Dumont, dans son discours lors de la soirée de première à Montréal. Écrite, adaptée et mise en scène par Anne Nozière, la pièce est une réflexion sur le monde des morts et des vivants et est jouée à la Maison Théâtre, près du Cégep du Vieux Montréal. On y suit le regard de Mustafa et Pamela, deux amis qui ont environ six ans et qui vivent le deuil.

items.leadExcerpt: Drawing fouls is a big part of basketball. It is an art form in itself. But players are beginning to take it too far, embellishing and dramatically flopping on the court in hopes of a whistle. The worst part is, they are getting away with it. The referees do not care, and they are willing to blow the whistle at any sign that a star player is struggling to create space or score. items.leadExcerpt: One of my favourite childhood memories is movie nights. Every Saturday, the whole family would gather around the TV with popcorn and hot chocolate, then choose a movie to watch from our CD/DVD binder. I have fond memories of going to the CD/DVD store with my parents. They would purchase any movie I found interesting, and we would spend evenings organizing the CDs in the binders by collection and genre. Technology became more advanced as I grew up. We discarded CDs and DVDs, and our big collection turned into arts-and-crafts projects. Now everything is on streaming subscription-based platforms. We pay more across platforms than what we did to build our collections, and we don’t even own the physical media anymore.

items.author: Florence Robert
items.excerpt: As the cost of living continues to rise, access to affordable groceries has become an increasing struggle for post-secondary students. Between having to pay for rent, tuition, groceries and other living expenses, students are often left choosing between basic
items.leadExcerpt: As the cost of living continues to rise, access to affordable groceries has become an increasing struggle for post-secondary students. Between having to pay for rent, tuition, groceries and other living expenses, students are often left choosing between basic needs and the heavy demands of university life. A February 2025 survey conducted by Équiterre, a non-profit environmental organization, found that 44 per cent of students across six Quebec colleges experienced some form of food insecurity. The high prices of groceries are not the only problem. Limited time between classes and work, lack of cooking equipment and stigmas surrounding financial insecurity all contribute to food insecurity.

items.leadExcerpt: Image courtesy of Warsame Ahmed In a video that has now amassed over 5,000 views on Instagram, Short King Warsame poses in front of an elevator in a bright, patterned yellow polo shirt and black slacks. One hand in his pocket, he smiles bashfully for the camera, flashing a cheeky thumbs up. The caption reads, “3’9” with 6’ confidence” — which, in just a few words, sums up Warsame’s ethos. Many members of the McGill community know Short King Warsame from their Instagram Reels feeds. With thousands of views on each reel and just over 2,000 followers at the time of writing (though he’s aiming for 10,000 by the end of 2026), Warsame is well-known both on and off campus as a beacon of positivity on social media. His most popular posts feature light-hearted content, mostly football commentary and videos of him at house parties and social events like OAP. In each post, he wears his signature toothy smile; except, of course, in the videos where he’s lamenting his woes as a fan of Manchester United.

items.leadExcerpt: Courtesy of AMUSE The Association of McGill University Support Employees (AMUSE) is pushing for more consistent rules on discipline, scheduling, and paid hours, saying casual employees face varying practices across McGill departments. These concerns form part of its ongoing negotiations with the university, which most recently met with the union on October 5 to discuss disciplinary procedures, probation, and hiring practices, with several issues remaining unresolved. According to its bargaining team, AMUSE represents approximately 1,300 to 1,600 casual employees, employees hired on a temporary or occasional basis, at McGill. Its collective agreement expired on May 31, 2025. The union developed its bargaining strategy through member surveys conducted in 2024 and 2025, as well as a special general meeting in September 2025.

While employees have standard wages, the leadership team works on a volunteer basis. “Since this is a nonprofit, community is everything,” Dumouchel added. The Daily spoke with Kevin Dean, a longtime McGill professor and staple within the Montreal jazz scene. “[L’Entracte] is a very ambitious project, butit has great potential and they seem to be on the right track.” Dean, who has lent his Hammond B3 organ and piano to the venue, says he’s keen to help out where he can. “It would be nice to have three full-time jazz clubs in town.” A virtuosic trumpet player and band leader in his own right, Dean runs a Sunday organ night at the venue twice a month, and regularly collaborates with student musicians.

items.leadExcerpt: The Daily has often described itself as just that: an opportunity that enables students to partake in the processes of independent reporting and collaborative editing. Part of the Daily’s mission has always been to encourage students to develop a critical journalistic eye. Today, the art of refining those “philosophical, political, aesthetic, literary and social values” has been interrupted by the Artificial Intelligence (AI) models that have infiltrated our academic spaces. AI has significantly shaped the way McGill students across various faculties approach learning; whether in drafting, editing, researching, or coding. Hence, McGill, which only has loose guidelines for professors and no enforeceable university-wide policy, faces an epidemic of unconstrained AI usage.

items.leadExcerpt: While a midnight showing on Halloween is the classic experience, Rocky Horror productions are a year-round event. This year, for the first time, a collection of students, rather than any specific interest group or club, organized and hosted its very own live showing. On Friday, October 30 2026, I donned my costume (Magenta) and headed to the Rocky Horror live-showing in Leacock 132. Doors opened at 7:00 PM. Last-minute tickets were sold at the door, as well as individual prop bags. “The props that we [use] will definitely cause laughs,” said Potamia.

Because it’ s important to celebrate good people doing good things. Why is it so hard to reach out? It is a simple question but one that resonated deeply with Aidan Licoppe, the co- founder and head of technology of the R3ACH app. With a background in coding and machine learning, Licoppe started to think about in-person social connection more seriously during the second year of his master’s program in experimental medicine at McGill. items.leadExcerpt: It has been nearly a month since the Prize’s announcement, when I find myself conducting an interview of my own, and the irony of discussing his media attention is not lost on me. Journalists, myself included, seem keen to contextualize Carson’s win as a national achievement: she is only the nineteenth-ever Canadian Nobel Laureate, and only the second-ever in the category of literature. More important to me than Carson’s citizenship, however, is the Montreal of it all; interviewing MacLaren in McGill’s McCall MacBain Arts Building, I am thinking of all the times she may have walked these halls herself, in her time as a faculty member of the Department of Classics.

items.imageCredit: Photo : Jeangagnon / CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
items.leadExcerpt: Comme débutent toutes les belles histoires, rendons-nous dans le merveilleux monde des égouts. Ces vastes systèmes de tuyaux, de pompes, de calculs méticuleux des courants d’eau se voient confier deux des plus nobles missions. La première, et certainement la plus intuitive, est d’évacuer les eaux usées, afin qu’elles retrouvent leur état naturel dans nos rivières, nos lacs, nos mers et nos océans. La seconde, bien plus piégeuse, mais tout autant nécessaire, s’assure que toute eau contaminée par l’industrie humaine ne s’invite pas dans nos fragiles écosystèmes.

items.title: Questionner la réforme électorale au Québec
items.author: Grégoire-Hubert Ducas
items.excerpt: L’arrivée des élections provinciales replace la question de la réforme électorale au centre du débat québécois. Elle rappelle l’importance d’une démocratie saine, dont la transparence estompe les dérobades administratives de plusieurs élus.
